event_confirmation: Company 6-K exhibits 99.1 and 99.2 dated 2026-10-13: Q3 2026 unaudited results released before the US open on Tue 2026-11-17, after the Hong Kong close; board meeting 2026-11-16; webinar 06:00 ET. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001744676/000095010326015462/dp254872_ex9901.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001744676/000095010326015462/dp254872_ex9902.htm
conviction_note: The evidence points both ways. Against the stock: the name has sold three of its last four real prints by 9-25% (two of them beats), and the June QuestMobile data shows Kugou, Kuwo and QQ Music traffic falling faster while Soda Music grows. For the stock: it is about 8x forward earnings and 53% off its high, a full quarter of Ximalaya should lift reported revenue slightly above the USD consensus, and management said in August it is preparing another buyback, funded by RMB44bn of cash plus $1bn of notes raised in September. The findings sum to -0.7 and the scaled number is -0.63 (p_up 47 x abs 10.5); the two agree because the negative reaction history is the only lean with a track record.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus revenue US$1.35bn and non-GAAP EPS $0.22 (whisper $0.23) per Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-10 (https://finviz.com/news/420443/tencent-music-must-show-its-core-subscription-engine-can-outrun-ximalayas-flattering-math); Benzinga also lists Q3'26E revenue $1.35bn (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TME/earnings-forecasts). Two USD sources agree, but no RMB consensus was found. At the US$/RMB 6.79 convenience rate in TME's Q2 release, $1.35bn is about RMB9.17bn (+8.4% y/y on Q3 2025's RMB8.46bn), though the RMB equivalent depends on the rate analysts used. There is no company quarterly revenue guide for Q3. The March 2026 FY guide was about 2% below consensus (Nomura via https://www.itiger.com/news/2620285775); its absolute figure was not found. Findings that depend on the RMB conversion are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 31.16m ADS at the 2026-09-30 settlement with 3.7 days to cover (massive.com per search: https://massive.com/quote/tme). It was 31.9m at 2026-08-14 with 2.8 days to cover (FINRA via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/tme/short-interest/). On roughly 1.5bn ADS-equivalents that is about 2% of float, so the short is not crowded and no squeeze mechanism applies. The October settlement was not found. The baseline has skew_25d null, front-expiry put/call OI 1.11 and an event-implied move of 9.19%, but the ATM spread is 55% of mid, so the options say nothing reliable about direction. Run-up: 5d -5.92%, 20d +1.79%, -53.4% from the 52-week high, +14.0% from the 52-week low (Oct 2 low $7.74 per Benzinga).

Earnings Whispers puts the post-Q2 drift at +4.9% (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/tme). Sector ETF (KWEB) return over the same days: not found.
expectations.vs_targets: Spot $8.83 against a consensus target of $15.21 (nemo.money via search, undated, https://explore.nemo.money/en/stocks/TME). Targets were reset in March 2026: JPM $12, UBS $13, MS $13, Mizuho $23 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/mizuho-cuts-tencent-music-entertainment-group-nysetme-price-target-to-2300-2026-03-18/). Spot is below every dated target found.
expectations.whisper_or_buyside_bar: Earnings Whispers whisper EPS $0.23 against $0.22 consensus. The preview frames the real test as organic membership growth holding near last quarter's level, ads no worse than flat, and the gross-margin decline staying 'slight' (https://finviz.com/news/420443/tencent-music-must-show-its-core-subscription-engine-can-outrun-ximalayas-flattering-math, 2026-11-10).

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, the release has to show the core (ex-Ximalaya) membership business still growing mid-single digits or better, with no further deterioration in advertising and margins, and preferably a new buyback of meaningful size. A headline beat inflated by Ximalaya will not be enough.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q4 2026 revenue $1.28bn per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TME/earnings-forecasts); this is odd against seasonality (Q4 2025 > Q3 2025), so treat it as low quality
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY2026 revenue guide given 2026-03-17, about 2% below consensus (absolute figure not found); Q1 guide RMB7.9bn, met. On the 2026-08-11 call: no new numeric guide, H2 gross margin 'decreasing slightly year-over-year', FY net margin 'will go down slightly', opex up slightly (https://www.webull.com/news/15424387923198976)
next_guide.basis: TME gave no numeric guidance in May or August, and the August call kept a cautious qualitative frame (ad headwinds, light-user pressure), so the likeliest outcome is no numeric Q4 guide plus cautious commentary. A 2027 outlook is not expected until the March Q4 release.

findings.finding: Expectations are deeply reset. Spot $8.825 is 53% below the 52-week high, about 60% down over a year (Simply Wall St, 2026-11-03: $22.31 to $8.91), about 8.3x forward earnings (debelegger), and far below the ~$15 mean target. The stock went into the print -5.9% over five sessions, so the bar the market holds is lower than in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A low starting multiple did not stop the selling: the stock was already about $9-10 before the Q2 print and still fell 11.9%. The post-Q2 drift was +4.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The low multiple is itself the price. The finding is that the bar for a relief move is lower than at any print in the past year. If the market expected another leg down, the 5-day pre-print selloff would have pushed the stock back to the $7.74 October low and put/call OI would be skewed well above 1.11.
findings.independence: Valuation from https://www.debelegger.nl/en/stock/TME.US (forward P/E 8.3) and Benzinga's price history https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TME/charts (down 55% over a year, low $7.74 on Oct 2). Separate sources, same price series.

findings.finding: On confirmed releases (not the baseline's 6-K matcher), TME has sold three of its last four prints by 9.6-25%: Q3 2025 beat then -9.64% intraday; Q4 2025 guide miss -25%; Q1 2026 in line about -1.3%; Q2 2026 slight beat (revenue +$20m, EPS +$0.01) -11.92%. A consensus beat alone has not been bought.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: headline beats on 2025-11-12 and 2026-08-11 were both sold by about 10-12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Reaction history is not a fact about this quarter. It is a sign that holders sell this name on what the quarter reveals about core growth. Only a full-quarter Ximalaya headline beat would make this print look different, and that is exactly the kind of beat holders have discounted. If the market had decided the derating was over, the implied move would be well below the name's ~10% realised print moves rather than 9.2%.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 -25%: https://www.itiger.com/news/2620285775; Q3 2025 -9.64%: https://www.itiger.com/news/1123949293; Q2 2026 -11.92%: sealed baseline. Separate events.

findings.finding: Arithmetic on company figures: Ximalaya added RMB407m in the 43 days after the 2026-05-18 close, about RMB0.85-0.9bn at that run-rate for a full Q3. Ex-Ximalaya revenue grew about 1% in Q2 (RMB8.52bn vs RMB8.44bn). Q3 therefore lands near RMB9.3-9.4bn against the $1.35bn consensus (~RMB9.17bn at the 6.79 convenience rate): a headline revenue beat of roughly 1-2%, mostly inorganic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue beat by about 1.3% with the stock -11.9%; Q3 2025 beat with the stock -9.6%. Revenue beats have not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Earnings Whispers preview already calls Ximalaya's contribution 'flattering math'. The RMB conversion of the USD consensus is uncertain, so the size of any headline beat is too. If the full-quarter Ximalaya step-up were not already in the bar, consensus would sit near Q2's +6% growth rather than +8-13%.
findings.independence: The Q2 Ximalaya figure and the ~1% organic growth are confirmed independently by https://m.jiemian.com/article/15077937.html. The consensus figure comes from the Earnings Whispers preview.

findings.finding: QuestMobile June 2026 (reported around 2026-09-10/15): Soda Music MAU 167m (+68.7% y/y) is approaching QQ Music's 189m (-0.7% y/y, down from +6.1% in March). Kugou fell -10.7% y/y (worse than March's -6.3%), Kuwo -18.5%, Quanmin K Ge -29.7%. Traffic erosion at TME's light-user apps accelerated through the end of Q2, which pressures ad-supported revenue and light-user membership in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 print (-25%) turned on falling MAU and competition. The Q2 2026 call conceded ad headwinds and light-user pressure, and the stock fell 11.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: TME stopped disclosing MAU and paying users in 2026, so third-party traffic data is the only window on the core, and it is not on terminals. Against that, the competition story is widely known and the stock is at lows. If the market had fully priced accelerating erosion, the stock would not have drifted +5% after Q2. This is a proxy, not company data, and SVIP/high-value users were said to be unaffected.
findings.independence: The same QuestMobile June data appears at https://www.lanjinger.com/d/1789013592290576849 (2026-09-15), but both articles rest on one dataset. The March data at https://www.36kr.com/p/3796235964243201 shows the trend.

findings.finding: The 2026-08-11 call set a cautious H2 frame with no numeric guide: CFO said H2 gross margin will be 'decreasing slightly year-over-year', FY net margin 'will go down slightly' with EBITDA up, sales and operating expenses up slightly, and the ad-supported model 'experienced some headwinds'. No numeric Q4 guide is likely, and the cautious tone is likely to continue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The March 2026 guide miss (Q1 ~5% and FY ~2% below consensus) cost about 25%. The August cautious margin commentary went with -11.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Most of this sits inside what management already guided to, which is why it is sized small. What is not priced is any H2 margin decline steeper than 'slight', or a first 2027 comment. If the market expected a clean outlook, the targets would not have stayed reset at $12-13 since March.
findings.independence: The same call is summarised at https://statementdog.com/analysis/TME/earnings_calls/317107 (one document). The FY guide miss is at https://www.itiger.com/news/2620285775.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is high and management has signalled more. On 2026-08-11 the CFO said 'we're also preparing for another round of share buyback'. $600m remains under the $1bn 2025 program, which runs to March 2027 ($400m used, all in Q2 at about $9.2/ADS). Cash and investments were RMB44.2bn at June 30, and TME raised $1bn of 5.05%/5.65% notes in September 2026 for general corporate purposes. A new program announced with Q3 is plausible; $1bn would be roughly 7-8% of the market cap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $1bn 2025 program was announced with Q4 2024 results in March 2025 and the shares rose (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/encent-music-shares-rise-after-q4-earnings-beat/ch7kBUGRb23; the date is inferred from context). The Q2 2026 completion of $400m did not prevent -11.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Intent is public, but the size and timing are not. The notes raise debt capacity well beyond operating needs with RMB44bn of cash already in hand, which points to returns or M&A. If a large new buyback were priced, the stock would not be trading near Q2's average repurchase price of $9.2. The financing question has been asked: the proceeds are for general purposes, with no distress signal (the prospectus says 'no material adverse change' since June 30), so the notes are read as a positive or a zero.
findings.independence: The $1bn notes are in the 424B2 dated 2026-09-03 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001744676/000119312526382909/d87523d424b2.htm). Cash and the Q2 buyback are in the Q2 6-K. Earnings Whispers also notes management 'hinted at a new shareholder return program' (https://finviz.com/news/420443/tencent-music-must-show-its-core-subscription-engine-can-outrun-ximalayas-flattering-math).

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement: TME's 424B2 for the $1bn notes, dated 2026-09-03 (two months into Q3), states 'There has been no material adverse change in the financial or trading position of the Company since June 30, 2026.' This is the only company statement on Q3 trading found between the Aug 11 call and the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is boilerplate in a bond prospectus that equity holders rarely read. It rules out a Q3 collapse through early September but says nothing about growth. If the market feared a Q3 breakdown, the October low would have been retested into the print.
findings.independence: This is the same document as the notes in the capital finding (one 424B2), but a different fact.

findings.finding: QQ Music's official notice (2026-05-12) raised the list price of the Deluxe Green Diamond monthly card from RMB20 to RMB25, but promotional prices stayed unchanged and IT Home found the actual monthly card still at RMB20. ARPPU support in Q3 is minimal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier ARPPU-led membership growth (2024-25) did not protect the Q3 2025 print (-9.6%).
findings.why_not_priced: The change is a list-price adjustment only, so there is little to price. If effective prices had risen, membership growth guidance would have been raised in August, and it was not.
findings.independence: https://m.sohu.com/a/1021558056_122004016/ reports the same notice (one underlying notice).

findings.finding: Peer: NetEase Cloud Music Q2 2026 revenue was roughly flat y/y at RMB2.0bn (H1 +3.4%), with membership growth offset by 'monthly ARPPU dilution due to changes in the subscriber mix'. Industry pricing pressure from free/cheap tiers is visible at the number-two subscription player.
findings.link: Direct competitor in Chinese online music subscriptions, same product and the same users being contested by Soda Music. NetEase Cloud Music revenue is about a quarter of TME's music revenue. It reported Q2, not Q3, so this is a stale read-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TME's Q2 2026 print, with membership growth slowing to 8% including Ximalaya, fell 11.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a Q2 data point published in August, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it is the only direct-competitor subscription read available, and it shows ARPPU dilution rather than price gains.
findings.independence: The NetEase release at https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3944574/netease-announces-second-quarter-and-interim-2026-unaudited-financial-results is the same numbers in another document.

findings.finding: Counterparty: Universal Music Group's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-29) showed organic subscription revenue growth of +9.5% against an ~8.2% analyst estimate, helped by wholesale price increases ('Streaming 2.0'). Global subscription monetisation is healthy, but UMG gave no China or TME-specific figure.
findings.link: UMG licenses its recorded-music catalogue to TME (a supplier of content). The China share of UMG subscription revenue is not disclosed, and UMG's growth is driven mostly by Western DSP price rises, so the transmission to TME is weak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of TME reacting to a UMG print found.
findings.why_not_priced: Out-of-market read-through. For a supplier, rising wholesale prices are, if anything, a cost item for TME. The size is near zero because no figure links it to TME's quarter.
findings.independence: The earnings-call detail at https://www.musicbusinessworldwide.com/supercharged-downtowns-margins-and-more-cost-cuts-what-i-learned-from-umgs-q3-earnings/ comes from the same company event.

outside_window.finding: The FY2026 annual dividend is normally declared with the Q4 results in March (FY2025: $0.24/ADS, ~$370m, declared 2026-03-17 per the 424B2). Any dividend increase resolves then, not at this print, unless a special distribution is announced on 2026-11-17.

Hong Kong shares (1698.HK) first react on 2026-11-18, because the results are uploaded after the HK close on 2026-11-17. This does not affect the US window but could feed back into ADS trading after it.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (null, with a 55%-wide spread). The 5-day run-up is negative (-5.9%), which fits the low-bar positive, while the name's own record of selling prints fits the negative. The set is near-balanced and slightly negative.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar): consensus exists only in USD from two agreeing sources and its RMB conversion is uncertain, so the consensus_bar finding was capped from +0.4 to +0.2 and print_vs_bar_pct cut from +1.5 to +1.0.
Lesson 6 and core table (lands inside what management already guided): the buyback intent was stated on the August call, so the capital finding fell from +1.5 to +1.0.

FPI lesson (reaction history from the wrong events): the baseline's 8-event history is 6-K operational noise (median 1.01%). Rebuilding from confirmed releases (-9.6, -25, -1.3, -11.9) raised abs_move_pct from 10 to 10.5, and the negative reaction history moved p_up from 48 to 47.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was checked before the negatives (~2% of float, 3.7 DTC); it is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk.

Lessons 1, 4, 5 and 9 left the other sizes standing: the reaction veto was already applied, the financing was already answered as a positive or zero, and the proxies were already filed small with independence noting they are proxies.
